timestamp_derivation: After migration 0080 was applied to stayconnect_site through the fail-closed runner, the grant verified as exactly SELECT, Policy History loaded live under the real svc_edged runtime role, and the binaries rebuilt and redeployed so the recorded head keeps describing them; before the author timestamp of the commit that introduces this receipt. After the merge commit 94c25c20 it describes. Per T0091, in the order T0108 requires.

merge.gates: All four required gates green on the exact head afbec858, first attempt. The Phase-5 log shows the restricted-role proof executing remotely: the granted role reads the ledger and is refused INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE.
merge.preflight: PASS on all seven default stages.

migration_applied.how: scripts/edge-migrate.sh on the appliance, --only 0080_the_service_may_read_the_ledger_it_writes --expect-db stayconnect_site --target-kind live-site --ack-target I_UNDERSTAND_LIVE_DARK_SITE_MIGRATION --expect-sha256 c9ac7886... --apply-role iam_v2_owner. Result: EDGE_MIGRATE_OK applied=1 skipped=0, under the bounded advisory lock.
migration_applied.file_identity: The shipped file's SHA-256 was compared on the appliance against the repository byte for byte before the runner was invoked, and the runner independently required the same digest as its binding pre-apply control.
migration_applied.role: iam_v2_owner is NOLOGIN by design, so the runner connects as a login role and SET ROLEs to it. SET ROLE grants nothing it did not already have, and every least-privilege check evaluates current_user after the switch.
migration_applied.result: has_table_privilege(svc_edged, iam_v2.checkout_grace_policy_publications, SELECT) = true, and information_schema.role_table_grants shows exactly one privilege_type for that role on that table: SELECT. No INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE. Ledger head is now 0080.

policy_history_proven_live.before: HTTP 500, then (after T0152) 200 with available=false and 'the service account cannot read the publication ledger on this appliance'.
policy_history_proven_live.after: HTTP 200, available=true, four versions, each with its actor, its bounded reason code and ITS OWN policy snapshot -- version 2 still reports 1800 seconds although version 3 restored 3600. Read through the same endpoint the browser uses, by the running edged process, under the real svc_edged role.
policy_history_proven_live.edged_error_count: Zero since the restart. The permission-denied diagnostic added in T0152 no longer fires, which is the runtime confirmation that the grant is what was missing.

a_real_operator_used_the_feature.what: The history shows a version 4 this delivery did not publish: 8 hours, 5 devices, reason HOTEL_ADMIN_UPDATE, published 2026-09-17T08:48:10Z by Site Admin through Hotel Admin.
a_real_operator_used_the_feature.why_it_is_recorded: It is the first policy the hotel chose for itself rather than one published to prove the mechanism, and it is the strongest evidence the mission succeeded: the workflow was used by an operator, unaided, to change what departing guests receive. It is left exactly as published -- reverting a Product-Owner decision to restore a test value would be the opposite of the point.
a_real_operator_used_the_feature.supersedes: The instruction earlier in this mission to end on fallback-identical terms. That was a constraint on evidence-publishing by the agent; the Product Owner has since made the commercial choice directly.

guest_impact.entitlements: Eight live grace entitlements, all still exactly 3600 seconds -- issued under earlier versions and untouched by three subsequent publications. Publishing reaches forward only, proven again on real rows.
guest_impact.conversions: Two real departing guests have been served by the published policy (trigger=CHECKOUT_GRACE, is_emergency=false, CHECKOUT_GRACE_V1). Zero emergency fallbacks.
